Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509
X.509 client certificate authentication: a certificate presented on a dedicated TLS port, or forwarded by a trusted reverse proxy in a header, signs in the user it is bound to (by the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate) at POST /login/x509, the form of the login page, with the CSRF token. Everything is off unless authserver.x509.enabled is true.

    Description
    AnyClientCertificateTrustManager
    The trust manager of the dedicated TLS port: it accepts any client certificate and advertises no certificate authority.
    CertificateController
    Manages the client certificates bound to the authenticated account (the operations of the contract).
    CertificateDtoMapper
    Maps the certificate bindings of the domain onto the DTO generated from the contract.
    CertificateExceptionHandler
    Answers the failures of the certificates API as application/problem+json.
    CertificatePrincipalExtractor
    Takes the SHA-256 fingerprint of the client certificate as the principal, as 64 lower case hexadecimal digits, which is what a binding stores and what ResolveCertificateLoginUseCase looks up.
    DevX509KeyStore
    Provides the server certificate of the dedicated TLS port when the dev profile is active and none is configured, so a developer does not have to create one: a self-signed certificate for localhost is generated once per machine with the JDK's keytool, stored in a key store under ~/.irurueta-auth-server/ that only the owner can read (its password in a file next to it, as DevKeyEncryptionSecret keeps its secret) and reused at every start.
    ForwardedCertificateFilter
    Reads the client certificate a reverse proxy that terminates TLS forwards in a header and leaves it where the servlet container leaves a certificate of its own, in the jakarta.servlet.request.X509Certificate request attribute, so the same X.509 filter and principal extractor serve both transports.
    InvalidCertificateException
    Thrown when the value sent to bind a certificate is not a single PEM X.509 certificate within its validity period.
    PemCertificateReader
    Reads the certificate sent to bind it to an account: exactly one X.509 certificate in PEM form, within its validity period, with a subject.
    PresentedCertificate
    What a binding keeps of a certificate sent to the account API: its fingerprint, which identifies it, and its subject, which only tells the bindings apart.
    X509AuthenticationSuccessHandler
    Completes a sign-in with a client certificate.
    X509ChainCustomizer
    Adds the sign-in with a client certificate to the login/UI chain through http.x509(...).
    X509ChainCustomizer.SessionStrategyConfigurer
    Hands the session authentication strategy of the chain to the success handler.
    X509Configuration
    Installs the sign-in with a client certificate in the login/UI chain, only while authserver.x509.enabled is true.
    X509Factor
    Registers the client certificate as an authentication factor: a strong primary one, because the holder proves possession of the private key during the TLS handshake (or the proxy did on the server's behalf), so a certificate satisfies the multi-factor policy on its own.
    X509ForwardedHeadersGuard
    Refuses to start when a certificate may be forwarded in a header while the server rewrites the address of its clients from the forwarded headers.
    X509LoginFilter
    The X.509 filter of the sign-in path.
    X509LoginMethodFragment
    Contributes the sign-in with a client certificate to the login page: a form with one button that posts, with the CSRF token, to POST /login/x509.
    X509Properties
    Configuration of the sign-in with a client certificate (authserver.x509.*).
    X509TlsConnectorCustomizer
    Adds the dedicated TLS port that requests a client certificate, when authserver.x509.port is set.
    X509TlsKeyStore
    The key store that holds the server certificate of the dedicated TLS port.
    X509TlsKeyStoreResolver
    Decides which key store holds the server certificate of the dedicated TLS port: the configured one or, under the dev profile and with none configured, the generated one.
    X509UserDetailsService
    Loads the account a client certificate is bound to.
